reasons.reason: Declines exact-stock guarantees and recommends scale and stock testing.
reasons.evidence:
Short answer: I can’t guarantee that what you design will print exactly as a specific paper stock you have, but this export is a standard digital PDF you can make compatible with your shop if you correctly set paper size and margins.

Here’s what’s practical:

- Export as a standard PDF (card sheets). You’ll need to set the paper size and printer margins in the print dialog to match what your print shop uses.
- Use “Actual Size” or “100%” if you’re looking to avoid scaling issues, and don’t rely on “Fit to page”.
- The service doesn’t impose any printer or shop-specific formats — it only exports card sheets. The on-paper result depends on your PDF, your printer settings, and your shop’s workflow.
- Before printing a full event series, export a small test folder and check the overall look on the paper you’ll use. That gives you a clear chance to tweak before full production.

If you tell me the paper size your shop enforces, I can walk you through how to set it up in the export and print dialog so everything aligns.
